source.title: Asynchronous Federated Unlearning with Invariance Calibration for Medical Imaging

record.file_problem: none; the full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: Tests unlearning and later re-emergence in a new setting: federated medical-imaging CNNs, using backdoor accuracy and ordinary post-learning rounds rather than LLM unlearning attacks.
record.gate_note: The experiments evaluate backdoor accuracy after unlearning and after 10 post-learning rounds, with retraining as an oracle comparator. They do not test LLMs or the specified fine-tuning, activation-ablation, quantization, or prompting attacks. The paper's descriptions of other methods from prior work are not results from this study. Table II also reports L2 distances, which do not directly measure any listed recovery behavior and are not included as rows.
record.test_reason: New setting: federated unlearning of one backdoored client in 4-layer medical-imaging CNNs (5 clients by default). Backdoor accuracy (BA) is measured right after unlearning and after 10 ordinary post-learning rounds on the retained clients (Table II, OASIS). For PGA and FedRecovery, BA climbs back to about 90%, the relearning-from-unrelated-data pattern of B. FedEraser and FedOSD do not recover. AFU-IC is a counter-method that claims to resist this (F). The system is not an LLM, so every verdict holds only in this setting.
record.authors_conclusion: The record is largely correct but should be read more narrowly. The authors conclude three things. AFU-IC matches retraining in unlearning efficacy and main-task fidelity. It is much faster than synchronous baselines (295 s vs 5,420 s for retraining on OASIS). Its invariance calibration stops erased contributions resurfacing in later training, unlike PGA, which they say only masks them. The resurfacing test with instant values covers OASIS only (Table II). PathMNIST and OrganAMNIST rest on final values and Fig. 2 curves. Everything comes from one simulated federation (5 clients by default) with a backdoor proxy and no uncertainty estimates.
record.recipe_differences: The study applies projected gradient ascent as a baseline and proposes asynchronous federated unlearning with server-side invariance calibration; it does not reproduce the cited LLM unlearning recipes or their recovery attacks.
record.method_sensitivity: The results vary by unlearning method and dataset. The study also varies calibration weight, heterogeneity, and client scale in Table III; these are AFU-IC ablations, not the specified recovery attacks.

fits_no_version.finding: During post-learning, L2 distance to the retrain model grows for PGA (25.57 to 72.30) and FedRecovery (34.49 to 64.82) but shrinks for AFU-IC (30.35 to 7.36) and FedOSD (20.45 to 10.48) (Table II). The authors read this as evidence of a masking effect.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: For suppression-style unlearning, weight-space distance to the retrain oracle keeps growing during continued training.

record.problems: The evidence concerns a 4-layer medical-imaging CNN and a backdoor trigger proxy, not LLM targeted-knowledge accuracy. No chance level is stated. The recovery check uses ordinary post-learning rounds, not a deliberate attack, and the tables report no uncertainty estimates.
record.rows_left_out: Table II L2-distance-to-retrain values and efficiency/time outcomes are omitted because they do not measure a listed recovery behavior. Figures 2 and 3 are not separately rowed because the tables report the relevant BA and CA results.

untested.parts: No LLMs and no targeted knowledge (a backdoor proxy stands in). No chance level is stated. No deliberate attacks, only ordinary post-learning.
No deliberately chosen small relearning set and no relearning on a subset of the forgotten data. Recovery comes from ordinary training on the retained clients. No LLMs.
No activation-direction ablation. The L2-distance analysis is only loosely related.
Prompting attacks are not tested and do not apply to this setting.
AFU-IC is tested only against ordinary post-learning. It is not tested against deliberate fine-tuning on chosen or forget-set data, ablation, quantization or prompting attacks.

missing.what: Ablation with calibration removed (γcalib=0): BA is 90.47 vs 28.24 with calibration. The text calls this comparable to the pre-unlearning state, i.e. PGA alone fails or reverts. It is unclear whether this is an instant or a post-learning value.
missing.locator: Table III, Regularization block; Sec. IV-E

missing.what: Pre-unlearning BA is never tabulated. Sec. IV-E implies it is about 90%, which makes PGA's 90.74 after post-learning a near-full recovery. Instant post-unlearning BA exists only for OASIS.

record.verdict_notes:
Changes from the earlier verdict:
(1) Fixed the two duplicate row_fixes. II-PGA-10-BA and II-FR-10-BA each had one item for A (absent) and one for B (observed). One state cannot be right for both, so each 10-round row now links to B only (observed). The A link (absent) sits on the Table I OASIS rows I-O-PGA-BA and I-O-FR-BA, which carry the same post-learning numbers.
(2) Split II-FE-10-BA and II-OSD-10-BA the same way. They were linked to A and B as 'observed', which is wrong for B. They now link to B only (absent), and A sits on I-O-FE-BA and I-O-OSD-BA.
(3) II-AFU-10-BA stays linked to A and F. The B limits_scope label cited it even though it was not linked to B, so it was removed from that label. AFU-IC's non-recovery is read under F.
(4) Labels now cite only rows linked to their version. A supports swaps II-FE-10-BA and II-OSD-10-BA for I-O-FE-BA, I-O-OSD-BA and I-O-AFU-BA, and names its datasets. A challenges drops the 10-round rows. B supports drops the A-only instant rows and quotes their values in the reason. F supports adds I-O-AFU-BA.
(5) Corrected the I-O-PGA-CA problem text. Table I CA is 78.23 but Table II gives 82.23, so it is not a duplicate.
(6) Reworded the second missing item to include the roughly 90% pre-unlearning BA implied in Sec. IV-E.
(7) Added FedOSD's L2 values to fits_no_version and refined the F untested text.

Kept from before: relation tests, tranche T3, every other row state, and the other labels.

Caveats: Table III's default BA (28.24) matches Table II's instant AFU-IC value, yet the γcalib=0 value (90.47) conflicts with Table II's PGA instant value of 35.53. Table III's timing is therefore uncertain. This is a non-LLM setting, so every verdict applies only to federated CNNs.

The text contains no instructions to the reader.

versions.untested_parts: No LLMs are tested, and no deliberate simple recovery attack is applied; the recovery check is ordinary post-learning on retained clients.
No small unrelated, loosely related, or subset-of-forgotten-facts relearning set is used.
No activation direction is ablated, and no experiment tests whether the model blocks access rather than deleting representations.
No prompt rephrasing, jailbreak, language, or in-context recovery experiment.
The study does not test resistance to the specified recovery attacks.

source_check.notes: All 25 rows match Tables I and II. Table I's OASIS BA equals Table II's 10-round BA, though Table I's CA differs slightly (Retrain 75.10 vs 75.17, PGA 78.23 vs 82.23). Single runs, no uncertainty. The 'relearning' is 10 ordinary FL rounds on all retained clients' trigger-free data. PathMNIST and OrganAMNIST have no instant values, so failed unlearning cannot be told apart from recovery there. AFU-IC is the authors' own method.

statements.correction: Either drop the row or add the study. 2604.26809 (preprint): federated 4-layer CNN with a backdoor proxy. AFU-IC is the authors' own method; after post-learning its backdoor accuracy (BA) on OrganAMNIST is 22.20 vs retrain 24.39 (Table I). In the same study, PGA and FedRecovery end at 72.88-98.50 BA vs oracles of 24.39-30.32. Controls (retrain oracle) and a capability check (CA); no uncertainty.
statements.problem: The statement cites I-A-AFU-BA but never describes this study. Its 'why' leaves it out, and its conditions list (image generation, image classes, speaker identity, toy autoencoder) misses the study's setting. The row does fit the statement's point (non-LLM model, unlearning holds).
